Collapses all groups in this category.
Expands all groups in this category.
The number of extra chunks claimed around every structure's bounding box for overlap prevention. Set to 0 to disable padding.

The mode based on how the distance from the world center is measured.

Circle: Distance is measured as a radius in every direction, creating a circular area around the world center.

Square: Distance is measured along the X and Z axes, creating a square area around the world center.
The structure will only generate if it is farther than the specified min. distance from the world center.
The structure will only generate if it is closer than the specified max. distance from the world center.
Whenever to override overlap padding from global or „%s“ namespace settings with specific settings of the „%s“ structure.
The number of extra chunks claimed around the structure's bounding box for overlap prevention. Set to 0 to disable padding.

The mode based on how flatness check checks for height differences.

Auto: Max. height difference is calculated automatically per each structure area and number of pieces.

Manual: Max. height difference is specified by the input field below.
The maximum allowed height difference between the highest and lowest terrain positions within the checked area. Structures will only generate if the terrain variation does not exceed this value.

The type of the height provider.

 - Constant: Specify a constant height
 - Uniform: Random value in a uniform distribution
 - Biased To Bottom: Random value, biased towards the bottom
 - Very Biased To Bottom: Random value
 - Trapezoid: Random value, isosceles trapezoidal distribution

The type of vertical anchor.

 - Absolute: An absolute height as seen on the F3 screen
 - Above Bottom: A relative height starting at the bottom of the world
 - Below Top: A relative height starting at the top of the world. Higher values move the height down
Numeric height used by the selected anchor type — either absolute Y level or offset from the world bottom/top.
Lowest possible height (absolute Y or offset from bottom/top, depending on anchor type).
Highest possible height (absolute Y or offset from bottom/top, depending on anchor type).
Controls how strongly heights are biased toward the bottom, higher values increase the chance of lower heights.
Width of the flat middle range where heights are evenly distributed, larger values widen this range.
Structure's starting height to match the terrain surface after initial placement.
Weight represent the chance of being chosen over others. Bigger weight means higher chance of being chosen.

Placement attempts is the number of positions tried when placing a structure within its placement region. When the structure cannot generate at its original position (for example due to unsuitable biomes or failed checks), additional deterministic positions within the same region are tried and the first valid one is used.

 - 1: vanilla behavior, only the original position is tried
 - > 1: failed structures get additional chances to generate
